statement: You are given an array dimensions of length n + 1 describing a chain of n matrices: matrix i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n, has dimensions dimensions[i − 1] × dimensions[i].
Multiplying an a × b matrix by a b × c matrix costs a × b × c scalar multiplications. Choosing where to put the parentheses changes the total cost.

Return the smallest total cost of multiplying the whole chain. This entry evaluates the same partition recurrence as Matrix Chain Multiplication: the best cost of a range is its cheapest split point plus the cost of joining the two halves.
